newsitem.title: NIGER: Electricity strike blacks out much of Niger.
newsitem.headline: Electricity strike blacks out much of Niger.

text.p: A two-day strike by electricity workers in Niger blacked out much of the West African country on Monday, disrupting water supplies and shutting factories.

Residents said electricity supply to the capital Niamey was cut at 5.00 a.m (0400 GMT) by workers of state power utility Nigelec who joined a growing protest against privatisation of government firms.
There was no immediate word on the effect of the stoppage on uranium mines in Niger's remote north.
Prime Minister Ahmadou Cisse declared on Sunday his government would press on with privatisation and other economic reforms agreed with Western donor agencies.
"The government intends to pursue the reform of industries and will not yield to pressure from labour unions," Cisse told a news conference.
